title: Regateando
desc: Arguing about price without being rude

sn.s: En el mercado nada tiene precio escrito.
sn.e: In the market nothing has a written price.

sn.s: El precio está en la boca del vendedor.
sn.e: The price is in the seller's mouth.

sn.s: Y el precio cambia según quién pregunta.
sn.e: And the price changes depending on who is asking.

sn.s: Roberto me lleva a comprar una camisa.
sn.e: Roberto takes me to buy a shirt.

sn.s: Yo veo una camisa que me gusta.
sn.e: I see a shirt I like.
"How much?" I ask.
"Two hundred," the seller says.

sn.s: Yo digo que sí y saco la plata.
sn.e: I say yes and take out my money.
Roberto grabs my hand.
"No," he says quietly. "Wait."
Roberto talks to the seller.
"That's dear, man," Roberto says.
"It's a good shirt," the seller says.
"Yes, but it's dear."
"How much do you want to pay?" the seller asks.
"A hundred and twenty," Roberto says.

sn.s: Eso es un poco más de la mitad.
sn.e: That is a bit more than half.
The seller pulls a face.
"I can't. A hundred and eighty."
"A hundred and forty," Roberto says.
"A hundred and sixty and it's yours."
"A hundred and fifty," Roberto says.

sn.s: "Ciento cincuenta y es mi último precio."
sn.e: "A hundred and fifty and that's my last price."
"Dale pues," Roberto says.
I pay a hundred and fifty.

sn.s: Ahorré cincuenta pesos en dos minutos.
sn.e: I saved fifty pesos in two minutes.
Outside Roberto explains it to me.

sn.s: "El primer precio nunca es el precio."
sn.e: "The first price is never the price."
"The first price is to start with."

sn.s: "Uno ofrece la mitad o un poco más."
sn.e: "You offer half or a bit more."
"And then you come together."

sn.s: "¿Y si dice que no?", pregunto yo.
sn.e: "And if he says no?" I ask.
"Then you walk away slowly."

sn.s: "Si el precio era posible, lo llaman."
sn.e: "If the price was possible, they call you back."

sn.s: "Y si no lo llaman, era su último precio."
sn.e: "And if they do not, it was their last price."

sn.s: Pero Roberto me dice algo más importante.
sn.e: But Roberto tells me something more important.
"Bargaining is not fighting."

sn.s: "Uno regatea con respeto y con broma."
sn.e: "You bargain with respect and with a joke."
"The seller has to end up happy."

sn.s: "Si el vendedor se enoja, uno regateó mal."
sn.e: "If the seller gets angry, you bargained badly."

sn.s: Después me dice dónde no se regatea.
sn.e: Then he tells me where you do not bargain.

sn.s: En la pulpería no se regatea.
sn.e: At the pulpería you do not bargain.

sn.s: En la fritanga no se regatea.
sn.e: At the fritanga you do not bargain.

sn.s: En el bus no se regatea.
sn.e: On the bus you do not bargain.

sn.s: El precio de la comida es el precio.
sn.e: The price of food is the price.

sn.s: Se regatea la ropa y las cosas.
sn.e: You bargain over clothes and things.

sn.s: Se regatea el taxi antes de subir.
sn.e: You bargain the taxi before getting in.

sn.s: Se regatea en el mercado grande.
sn.e: You bargain in the big market.

sn.s: La semana siguiente lo hago solo.
sn.e: The next week I do it on my own.
I want to buy a bucket.
"How much is the bucket?" I ask.
"Eighty," the seller says.
"That's dear," I say. "Fifty?"
"Seventy," she says.
"Sixty and I'll take it."

sn.s: La señora se ríe y me lo deja en sesenta.
sn.e: The woman laughs and lets me have it for sixty.
"The chele has learned," she says.

sn.s: Y eso me gusta más que los veinte pesos.
sn.e: And I like that more than the twenty pesos.
